text:
kevin: Quick sync — followup on private/VPC CP split. We discussed letting the tenant connector (agent) terminate mTLS for control/data plane inside customer VPC and only use a shared egress relay for hard failover. Two open concerns: (1) pressure on our SNAT pool if many tenants failover concurrently, (2) trust model + cert rotation for connectors. Thoughts?

anita: I still prefer a tiny CP-side mutual-auth proxy to validate connector claims before we accept traffic. If we fully trust the connector, we need clear attestation and a short lived identity. Otherwise we leak auth surface.

dmitri: Agreed on short-lived identities. Proposed: agent bootstraps via customer OIDC -> exchanges for a short-lived client cert (24h). CP keeps a small verification proxy for handshake only (SNI+client cert check) but does NOT terminate or proxy actual customer egress—agent keeps data flow local. This preserves proof-of-possession while avoiding unnecessary hairpin.

kevin: That hybrid sounds plausible. For SNAT pressure we should avoid a blunt fallback that sends traffic to shared-relay for every connector failure. Instead: implement graduated fallback policy: (A) transient failure (<30s): buffer/retry locally, (B) mid window (30s-5m): queue control-plane requests and do best-effort background reconnection, (C) sustained failure (>5m): switch to shared-relay but mark tenant as "relayed" and apply IP-limiting heuristics.

lia: What are the heuristics? We need practical limits to avoid exhausting SNAT IPs. Suggestion: per-tenant cap on concurrent relayed flows (default 5), global relay ingress QPS cap, and a reclaim loop that kicks idle relayed flows after 10m. Also keep a soft-limits alert at 70% SNAT capacity and hard stop at 95%.

product-amy: From product perspective we must communicate behavior to customers. Two billing options: inclusive fallback (we absorb short relays up to X minutes/month) or pay-per-ephemeral-ip which reserves a /32 for tenant during fallback windows. Need a default (inclusive up to 60m/month?) and an opt-in for paid reservation. Add to docs.

dmitri: Telemetry: emit metric `tenant.egress.fallback.state{tenant_id,reason}` with states: local, retrying, queued, relayed, forced-relay. Emit counters for `tenant.egress.fallback.count` and histograms for `tenant.egress.relay.duration`. Add tag `snat_pool_pressure` to global metrics.

kevin: Good. We also need reason codes in logs: agent_unreachable, bootstrap_failed, cert_expired, auth_mismatch, nat_quota. Ops should be able to filter by reason in Console.

anita: Runbook notes: if SNAT pool soft-limit hit -> temporarily raise idle reclaim aggressiveness and start rebalancing tenants with dedicated egress. If hard-limit hit -> auto-disable new relay allocations and failover only for tenants with critical SLA tag. Manual override via Console toggle `allow-relay-overflow` for narrow ops use.

ops-bot: infra-bot: canary rollout scheduled: 50 tenants on cp-split-handshake v1 in us-east-1 at 2024-06-10T11:00Z. Auto-rollback if `tenant.egress.relay.duration` p95 > 2s or `snat_pool_utilization` > 0.8 for >5m.

lia: Security: Avoid static bootstrap tokens. Implement OIDC-based bootstrap + short lived certs + cert rotation alarms at 80% of validity window. Also record CRL-like revocation list in CP for immediate connector bans.

dmitri: Handshake sketch for developer notes: agent calls CP `/v1/bootstrap` with OIDC token, CP verifies and returns client cert + CA bundle and `egress_preference`. Agent exposes `/health/egress` locally containing `status: ok|degraded|down`, `last_checked`, `fallback_count`. Example: {
  "status":"degraded",
  "last_checked":"2024-06-10T10:58:04Z",
  "fallback_count":1
}

kevin: Canary plan: start 50 tenants, watch `tenant.egress.fallback.count`, `snat_pool_utilization`, and customer error rates. If we see >10% of canary tenants in `relayed` for >10m, pause. Kill switch: Console feature flag `cp-split:force-disable-relay` that immediately blocks new relays and signals agents to stay in queued/retry mode. Need runbook owner.

product-amy: Action items: add billing options to pricing doc, add default tenant-level relayed cap, and customer-facing FAQ.

anita: Dev action: prototype OIDC bootstrap + cert issuance service + lightweight CP verification proxy. Add unit tests around cert expiry and revocation.

dmitri: Observability action: add metrics and alert rules, implement telemetry reason tags, wire Console filter.

lia: Ops action: implement reclaim loop + SNAT capacity thresholds + runbook entries for soft/hard limits.

kevin: I'll coordinate with Security and SRE. If no objections by EOD Friday we'll cut a spike branch and schedule the canary for next week. Quick thumbs? :thumbsup:
